knowledge:
- key_parameters: dataset=The input file containing probe name, chromosome, position, and LRR/BAF values ;; output_file_name=The base file name used to save the text and HTML results ;; beta=Scale parameter jump threshold for segmentation (default 0.5; 0 gives probe-level segmentation, larger values give coarser segmentation) ;; min_region_bp_size=Minimum size in base pairs for reported regions (default 1000) ;; classification=If TRUE, multiple testing correction is performed (default FALSE) ;; loss_threshold=LRR threshold to classify deletions (default -0.2) ;; gain_threshold=LRR threshold to classify amplifications (default 0.2; note: documented as loss_threshold default 0.2 due to a typo in the PDF) ;; baf=Logical indicating if BAF measurements are available for LOH detection (default TRUE) ;; loh_threshold=Threshold to distinguish homozygous/heterozygous genotypes (default 0.75) ;; loh_frequency=Minimum fraction of homozygous probes to mark a region as LOH (default 0.8) ;; bs=Number of permutation bootstraps for null distribution (default 1000) ;; pval_threshold=Significance level to reject the null hypothesis (default 0.05) ;; html=Logical to generate an HTML summary of detected regions (default TRUE) ;; getGenes=Logical to generate an HTML summary of overlapping genes (default TRUE) ;; mart_database=BioMart database name (default "ensembl") ;; ensembl_dataset=BioMart dataset used to get information from Ensembl BioMart database (default "hsapiens_gene_ensembl")
- alternatives: PennCNV (mentioned as a tool that produces LRR and BAF raw files, which VegaMC can integrate with) ;; VEGA (variational segmentation algorithm upon which VegaMC's segmentation is based)
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing a cohort of disease-affected patients with aCGH or SNP array data (specifically LRR and BAF) to identify recurrent, statistically significant driver chromosomal imbalances (deletions, amplifications, LOH) while filtering out passenger mutations.
- pitfalls: Input data must be sorted by genomic position within each chromosome; if the input is unsorted (e.g., direct output from PennCNV), sortData must be run first to avoid incorrect segmentation ;; LOH detection requires BAF measurements; if BAF is missing, baf must be set to FALSE to avoid errors ;; The LRR and BAF columns for each sample must be ordered strictly as LRR followed by BAF.

workflows.name: chromosomal_imbalance_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify driver chromosomal imbalances (deletions, amplifications, LOH) from sorted or unsorted aCGH/SNP array data.
input: breast_Affy500K.txt (Tab-delimited file containing probe name, chromosome, genomic position, and LRR/BAF values per sample)
gist.txt (Unsorted tab-delimited file containing probe name, chromosome, genomic position, and LRR/BAF values per sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Sort the input dataset by genomic position using sortData (required if data is unsorted, e.g., raw PennCNV output) ;; 2. Run the joint segmentation, classification, and significance testing using vegaMC ;; 3. Retrieve the results matrix and view the column names
workflows.code:
library(VegaMC)

file.copy(system.file("example/breast_Affy500K.txt",
    package="VegaMC"),".")

results <-
vegaMC("breast_Affy500K.txt",
	output_file_name="breast.analysis",
	beta=1,	min_region_bp_size=2000, bs=5000,
	html=FALSE, getGenes=FALSE)

colnames(results)

sortData("gist.txt", "gist.sorted.txt")

gist.results <-
    vegaMC("gist.sorted.txt",
            output_file_name="gist.analysis.default",
            min_region_bp_size=1000)
